📰 General

U.S. Mint Ends Production of the One-Cent Coin After 217 Years •

The U.S. Mint ceased production of the one-cent coin on Wednesday, marking the end of its circulation after 217 years. The decision, finalized six months prior by the Trump administration, stemmed from the significant cost of manufacturing pennies, which had risen to nearly four times the coin’s value. The last penny produced will still be legal tender, though its use is expected to decline as retailers increasingly opt not to accept it. The move reflects a broader trend in the U.S. of eliminating smaller denominations due to economic factors.

🌍 World

Israel Plans to Deport Seriously Ill Palestinian Teenager Back to Gaza •

Israeli authorities intend to deport Yamen Al-Najjar, a 16-year-old Palestinian suffering from a chronic illness, back to the Gaza Strip. Al-Najjar, who requires specialized medical care, is currently receiving treatment in an Israeli hospital. Doctors and his mother express grave concerns about his well-being if he is returned to Gaza, where access to adequate medical facilities is severely limited. The move has drawn international condemnation and raised questions about Israel’s commitment to providing humanitarian aid to Palestinians.

🦅 US

Northern Lights Visible Across 18 US States Wednesday Night Due to Geomagnetic Storm •

A strong geomagnetic storm has created conditions for northern lights sightings across a wide swath of the United States. The event, visible Tuesday night, offered opportunities for viewing in states including Oregon, Washington, and Montana. Cloudy skies in some areas hampered visibility, but clear conditions in many locations allowed for observation of the aurora borealis. Experts predict continued activity may provide further chances for viewing throughout the night.

💰 Business

Delta CEO Bastian Reports Operational Recovery Following Air Traffic Control Disruptions •

Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian addressed a CNBC interview on November 12th, detailing the airline’s operational recovery following significant disruptions caused by Air Traffic Control issues. The airline confirmed its operations are now stable, with employees focused on assisting customers impacted by cancellations and delays. Bastian emphasized that safety remains the company’s primary concern during the period of instability. Delta is continuing to work with Air Traffic Control to minimize further disruptions and restore normal flight schedules.

💻 Technology

Valve Unveils the Steam Machine: A New Challenger in Gaming Hardware •

Valve is launching the Steam Machine, a new gaming console designed to compete directly with Microsoft’s Xbox and Sony’s PlayStation. The device boasts custom-designed hardware, including a Snapdragon 845 processor, 8GB of RAM, and a 64GB SSD. Valve emphasizes the console’s focus on a streamlined, curated gaming experience, prioritizing Steam’s existing library and services. The Steam Machine will initially launch with a price of $399, offering a unique alternative for PC gamers seeking a dedicated console experience.

🎭 Entertainment

Zendaya Dominates Met Gala, Showcasing Stunning Custom Valentino Gown •

Zendaya attended the 2024 Met Gala, held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City. She wore a custom-designed white Valentino gown featuring a dramatic, sculpted silhouette and intricate feather detailing. The gown was praised by fashion critics and social media users alike for its innovative design and Zendaya’s confident presentation. The actress posed for photographers throughout the evening, solidifying her status as a major fashion icon.

🏅 Sports

Kansas Jayhawks Lead 2026 Recruiting Class, Several Programs Poised for Ascent •

The Kansas Jayhawks currently hold the top-ranked recruiting class in the nation for the 2026 season, marking the first time this has occurred in 247Sports’ history. Their class boasts commitments from Taylen Kinney, Trent Perry, Davion Adkins, and Luke Barnett. Duke, Arkansas, and Michigan State are among the programs identified as potential contenders to significantly move up the rankings. These teams are actively pursuing top talent, aiming to bolster their rosters for the upcoming college basketball season.

🔬 Science

Scientists Propose Radical Explanation for Unusually Large Black Hole Merger •

Recent data from the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO) revealed a black hole merger significantly larger than predicted by current models. Physicists are now investigating a potential explanation involving a “seed” black hole formed from a dense star. This seed could have rapidly accreted matter, growing into the unexpectedly massive black hole observed. The discovery challenges existing theories about black hole formation and evolution.

🩺 Health

Microwaving Plastic: Experts Reveal Potential Risks and Safe Alternatives •

Recent research highlights the potential dangers of microwaving certain types of plastic containers. The article details that many plastics, even those labeled “microwave-safe,” can release harmful chemicals like phthalates and BPA when heated. These chemicals can then leach into food, posing potential health risks. Experts recommend using glass, ceramic, or specifically labeled microwave-safe plastics made from polypropylene as safer alternatives for heating food in the microwave.
